Simple - Warm - Dark

Simple warm dark lakes are characterized by simple fish communities, typically with fewer than 4 different groups of sportfish (e.g., panfish and some bass or northern pike). Water temperatures tend to be warmer than average, and water is less clear than average. They tend to be small in surface area.  This is the most common class of lake in Wisconsin, with 1,650 simple warm dark lakes  scattered across all parts of the state.
Simple warm dark lakes can provide great opportunities for action for black crappie, and often also support bluegill and largemouth bass. They rarely have any walleye or muskellunge.

Simple - Harsh - Has Fishery

Simple harsh lakes are lakes where extreme conditions, typically winterkills, limit what fish can survive. They are broken into two categories: "has fishery" and "no fishery". This lake is in the "simple harsh - has fishery" class, which can have 1-2 types of sportfish present. They are very small in surface area. There are 613 of these lakes scattered around the state.
"Simple harsh - has fishery" lakes may have some panfish, particularly yellow perch, and can be dominated by bullheads.
Chilton Millpond 75
Simple - Riverine

Simple riverine lakes are characterized by simple fish communities, typically with fewer than 4 different groups of sportfish present (e.g., panfish and some bass or northern pike). Water tends to flow though these lakes quickly (on average less than 15 day residence-time) and they tend to be small in surface area - many of these are small millponds on warmwater streams. There are 175 simple riverine lakes in Wisconsin, scattered across all parts of the state.
Simple riverine lakes may have good action opportunities for smallmouth bass and quality opportunities for northern pike. They rarely have any walleye or muskellunge.

Simple - Harsh - No Fishery

Simple harsh lakes are lakes where extreme conditions, typically winterkills, limit what fish can survive. They are broken into two categories: "has fishery" and "no fishery". This lake is in the "simple harsh - no fishery" class where winterkills are frequently and lake pH is very low, so few fish can survive. They are very small in surface area. There are 1,059 of these lakes scattered around the state.
"Simple harsh - no fishery" lakes usually have not sportfish species present. Central mudminnow and small minnow species are typically the only species that can survive in these lakes.

This is the most common class of lake in Wisconsin, with 1,650 simple warm dark lakes  scattered across all parts of the state.

Simple - Trout Pond

Simple trout ponds are characterized by simple fish communities, typically with fewer than 4 different groups of sportfish present (e.g., panfish, bass, and trout). These tend to be shallow and small in surface area, and springs that provide incoming groundwater keep temperatures cold and suitable for trout. There are 308 simple trout ponds in the state, mostly in the northern part of the state and concentrated in and around Langlade county.
Simple trout ponds may have some warmwater species like bluegill, pumpkinseed, largemouth bass, or northern pike present, but also can support coldwater-dependent trout species.
